name: Brown Orange
lede: Brown Orange is a deep orange-brown, a descriptive name that shares its tone with iron oxide pigments and one rare brown-orange mineral.

sections.title: Between brown and orange
sections.body: The name sets [[brown]] against [[orange]], and the swatch sits between them: nearest ISCC-NBS name "deep orange" at a distance of 4.1 [1]. Our sources list it in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system and the 2010 xkcd survey [1]. Nearby named colors include [[dark-orange]], [[rust]] and [[ochre]].

sections.title: Iron oxides and akaganeite
sections.body: Iron oxide pigments include the ochres, siennas and umbers, and the synthetic Mars colors come in orange as well as black, brown and yellow [2]. The pigment books describe akaganeite, an iron hydroxide mineral, as brown, brown-orange or bright yellow; it is rare and forms from the weathering of iron-rich minerals [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 266 of our 23,781 paintings, 1.12 percent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1400s, found in 9 of the 945 paintings from that century, at 1.2 times the expected rate [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 78 percent of the 166 paintings that hold it [4].
